Event.EventText: Although the formal home team was Canada, the spectators were of course much preferring Nederland.
Canada had chosen a strategic [Replacement Error: Context 'formation' not found] formation.

The Canada goalkeeper today will be Tourrette, and trying to protect him will be Choi, Wolf and Ferguson in the defensive back-line.


The midfield is made-up of O'Connor, Trapani, Rummens, Johnson and Cooper, while Pemberton and Ife will be relied upon to score goals, and lots of them.
Nederland had chosen a strategic [Replacement Error: Context 'formation' not found] formation.

Nederland have Evers in goal today.


Hoekwater, van Oostrom, van Gompel and Evers will handle the defence.


In front of them Somers, Jassies, Dorenbos and Savelkoul will operate the midfield, setting up ten Berge and van Steenderen to spearhead the attack.

A Nederland player goes studs up on his opponent!
Sylvester van Oostrom wins the challenge but is rightly penalised.
The referee shows him the yellow card.

An interesting bit of build-up play beginning here ...
Some fans are rising from their seats in expectation...
Neil Pemberton looks like he is trying to find an opening...
He's gone for a speculative chip - the goalkeeper is scrambling back...
GOAL! The keeper's hand stretched out desperately but couldn't stop it beating him to make the score 1 - 0 to Canada.

The referee blows the whistle...
And that's all for the first half. The score so far 1 - 0.
This part of the game has been a stand-off between the teams.

Elegant corner kick by Freddie van Steenderen. It's firm, it's high, and it swerves in dangerously in front of the goal.
Goos Savelkoul wins the header from a standing start despite the attention of two defenders!
It's powerful and precise, but the goalkeeper chances in the right direction and can block it.
Still a very impressive display by Goos Savelkoul, such a dominating force in the air.

It's a continued push forward for Canada, this time on the right wing.
The home fans sense more goals in the making!
The Nederland are doing a good job covering the box, and the Canada winger is running out of options...
He lifts the ball into the area on the off chance someone will reach it.
It finds Scott Rummens, who nearly scores with a header! Unfortunately, it's tipped away by the keeper.

An interesting bit of build-up play beginning here ...
The away fans sense an opportunity, and get to their feet ...
From out left, Nederland floats a ball over the Canada defenders ...
Roel Dorenbos has his eyes firmly fixed on the ball. He hits it sweetly on the volley!
Goalkeeper reacts! No chance - GOAL! Sparks seemed to fly from the boot of Roel Dorenbos on contact! Beautiful strike!! We'll be watching that replay in the best of the month. It's all even now! 1 - 1.

A Canada midfielder embarks on a fine direct run down the inside.
He nears the edge of the Nederland box, where he's challenged by the defender.
He slips through, then lays it off to Neil Pemberton who instinctively goes for the half-volley.
So close! It brushes off the post, and wide!
Canada claimed to have seen most of the ball, and the statistics agreed with them - possession being 51 percent.

There are only a few seconds left of regular time and we have no winner as yet.
Since this match cannot end with a draw the referee is going to call for extra time.
And so he does! The players will have a quick refreshment on the sidelines before we kick off again.

Lovely interchange passing down the right-hand side here. It could lead to something interesting for Nederland...
The away terraces are holding their breath in the hope that this leads to something special...
This could be it! Nederland's fans are on their feet as this could be a breakthrough chance!
Oh Roel Dorenbos of Nederland should have buried that, but after 96 minutes he chased a through ball from the right, Jamie Tourrette was out as fast as a snake, grabbing the ball from right under his nose.

Extra time has come to an end and this game is still tied.


This will be decided by penalties!

Someone who is not likely to be affected by his nerves in a situation like this is Simon Ferguson, the Canada player...
Let's see what he can do here.
There it goes.
It's an interesting kick, but Klaas Evers manages to make the save! Good work by the keeper to keep the score at 1 - 1!

Someone who is not likely to be affected by his nerves in a situation like this is Freddie van Steenderen, the Nederland player...
Let's see what he can do here.
There it goes.
It's an interesting kick, but Jamie Tourrette manages to make the save! Good work by the keeper to keep the score at 1 - 1!

Canada's Horace Wolf to have a go from the spot here.
He walks up with a sly grin on his face. He looks like he means business!
He's put it wide!
He oozed attitude as he placed that penalty kick, he just didn't do it well enough.

It's time for Nederland's Roel Dorenbos to make the long walk to the spot.
What's this?
He looks like he's taunting the goalie!
The keeper stares back, unfazed - let's see if the taker has jinxed his own penalty...
Au contraire! He shows himself as the master of the situation and flicks it in to the right of a very frustrated keeper! 1 - 2.

It is time for Brian Trapani to make his mark for Canada.
The pressure is always on the penalty kick taker, but he looks like he can handle it.
It's well placed...
It's a stellar block by Klaas Evers! He just wouldn't let the ball in!

Nederland's Eelco Jassies to have a go from the spot here.
He walks up with a sly grin on his face. He looks like he means business!
He's put it wide!
He oozed attitude as he placed that penalty kick, he just didn't do it well enough.

It is time for Ian Johnson to make his mark for Canada.
The pressure is always on the penalty kick taker, but he looks like he can handle it.
It's well placed...
It's a stellar block by Klaas Evers! He just wouldn't let the ball in!

The referee signals that Nederland is next up.
Goos Savelkoul will be taking it.
What's going through his mind, I wonder? He is certainly taking his time preparing for this one...
It goes wide! The ball brushes the left post. The score is still 1 - 2. His nerves did him in!

It's time for Canada's Scott Rummens to make the long walk to the spot.
What's this?
He looks like he's taunting the goalie!
The keeper stares back, unfazed - let's see if the taker has jinxed his own penalty...
Au contraire! He shows himself as the master of the situation and flicks it in to the right of a very frustrated keeper! 2 - 2.

Someone who is not likely to be affected by his nerves in a situation like this is Sylvester van Oostrom, the Nederland player...
Let's see what he can do here.
There it goes.
It's an interesting kick, but Jamie Tourrette manages to make the save! Good work by the keeper to keep the score at 2 - 2!

It is time for John O'Connor to make his mark for Canada.
The pressure is always on the penalty kick taker, but he looks like he can handle it.
It's well placed...
And it's in of course! He keeps his cool, and now it is 3 - 2.

Someone who is not likely to be affected by his nerves in a situation like this is Keesje van Gompel, the Nederland player...
Let's see what he can do here.
There it goes.
It's an interesting kick, but Jamie Tourrette manages to make the save! Good work by the keeper to keep the score at 3 - 2!
The most important Canada player was Jamie Tourrette.
Horace Wolf was a disappointment, however.
The most dominating Nederland player was without a doubt Klaas Evers.
Goos Savelkoul on the other hand, had a terrible day.
The match ends 3 - 2.
As the referee started preparing for kick-off, a smattering of fireworks set off in the stands of the Soyboys fans, followed by song. After a short delay, the match could start as planned.

It is completely packed here at Stadio al Dente today!
Personally, I don't think the weather should matter to a real fan, but I know some only come out on a decent day like this. Becker Vargas is the appointed referee today, and they will be assisted by Romolo Dentesano and 崔 (Cui) 书简 (Shujian).
It's derby day, and all of Tallinn seems to have shut down due to this event!

The players have received their final instructions from the coaches and are now entering the field.
The referee is getting ready to start the game!

The Cacio goalkeeper today will be Arakcheev, and trying to protect him will be Justyna and Santarelli in the defensive back-line.


The midfield is made-up of Krupicki, Innes, Puga, Boujadi and Melnichenko, while Lokvenc, Tsapenko and Zeddelmann will be relied upon to score goals, and lots of them.

Here's the Soyboys lineup, then ...


In goal, Hõbemägi.


The defenders are Przydatek and Newsam.


In midfield, Uuttera, Alfonso, Laratore, 祖航 (Zuhang) and Marchetti.


And finally, in attack they have Fonrodona, Dzimiński and Bento.

The teams look to have come out with a similar approach to the game.
Both coaches have chosen a 2-5-3 formation.
The teams are in position, and the referee signals that the match can start. There's the kick off, and a huge cheer erupts around the ground. The game is on!

No clear favourite today, at least not judging by past results.
The last time these teams played it was a 0-0 draw, as you may remember.
It's been a positive start to the game for Cacio. They have more of the ball possession, and I think we can expect this to lead to attacking chances as well.

Soyboys drives forward through the middle.
A lucky bounce gifts 林 (Lin) 祖航 (Zuhang) a chance...
He takes it with aplomb, crashing a low shot toward the home team goalkeeper!
It's in! That makes it 0 - 1. The guests are in the driver's seat now. Heribert Fonrodona laid it on a plate with that delivery!

The teams are challenging each other to establish possession in central midfield.
The hosts are showing heart, despite their disappointments so far. Let's see here ...
Soyboys regains control of the ball, and immediately sends it high up the field.
It's actually a fabulous pass.
Salvatore Laratore receives it with perfect timing and has no trouble with placing it behind the goalkeeper. It's 0 - 2 now, and things are getting worse for Cacio. Heribert Fonrodona laid it on a plate with that delivery!

Heribert Fonrodona cuts in towards the goal from the right.
The Soyboys player strikes a curling left-foot shot from the edge of the area...
So close! But in a heroic effort, a defender manages to keep the ball from crossing the goal-line!

Paavo Hõbemägi is massaging his left knee with a worried look on his face.
He's up, testing a few tentative steps ...
It still hurts. He will need to come off.
The replacement for the injured player will be Richard Nõmmoja.
Soyboys's doctor confirms that Paavo Hõbemägi will need physical therapy for 1 week before he can play again.

Soyboys's Adam Newsam has a free-kick on the edge of the area.
He whips the ball into the box with a terrifying amount of in swing!
Adam Newsam starts to peel away in celebration...!
No, it's denied! Yuriy Arakcheev's big left hand stretches out and claws the ball clear. Stunning save!

The referee has seen something...
Natã Bento of Soyboys is shown the yellow card!
Unsportsmanlike behaviour!
Apparently he mouthed off pretty badly about something, with the referee just a few steps away. Not too bright, that lad.

The referee blows the whistle...
And that's all for the first half. The score so far 0 - 2.
Cacio had most of the ball, with 51 percent of possession.
The referee blows the whistle. It's time for the second half!
Now, let's see! 17417 came through the turnstiles today.

Look at Cacio’s Alessandro Santarelli run down the right side. He has his head up and a smile on his face. This means nothing but misery for the other team.
He motions a teammate through the middle of the midfield, passes the ball, then darts down the side waiting for the return pass.
There! The return pass is threaded perfectly through a defender’s wide stance and it’s collected cleanly ...
... juggled a bit, then lifted up and over the defender ...
... one more touch, and a SPECTACULAR BICYCLE KICK takes the ball right into the corner of the old onion bag! Renoir, Michelangelo, and Picasso never painted a better picture than that which Alessandro Santarelli has just painted! That helps the home team claw one back leaving the score at 1 – 2! Yurii Melnichenko pulled the strings in the build-up.

Alberto Marchetti plays a neat one-two near the penalty area ...
He breaks through!
The keeper shows impressive reflexes!
Goal! The keeper touches it, but it's a real cannonball and he can't hold on to it. 1 - 3.

Soyboys are looking really dangerous down their right hand side.
Heribert Fonrodona is calling for the ball! I think he fancies his chances.
This could be it! Great opportunity - he takes the shot...!
It's a really powerful shot ...
The keeper gets his hands on it but cannot hold on!
It's 1-4, and the home crowd is NOT impressed with what they just witnessed!
Cacio have had a great run in recent matches, but that dominance is nowhere to be seen today.

The referee will let play continue for an additional 2 minutes beyond the allotted 90.
This is, of course, compensation for injury time and other delays we have seen during the match.

This match is over.
The final result is 1 - 4.
The match is over! The Soyboys players are very happy, hugging each other and waving to their fans to thank them for their support.
Possession in this half belonged to Cacio, who controlled the ball 51 percent of the time.
The most dominating Cacio player was without a doubt Vlastimil Lokvenc.
Heribert Fonrodona performed admirably for Soyboys.
